title: Kepler-13A: TESS sector 14 light curve, as collected (SAP)
credit: TESS, sector 14 (NASA; SPOC light curve from MAST)

license.statement: NASA mission data, released through MAST without restriction on reuse. MAST asks that work using its data acknowledge the mission and the archive.

columns.name: time
columns.description: bin centre: t0 + (index + 0.5) x binDays, in BTJD

columns.name: flux
columns.description: SAP flux (all the light in the aperture) over its median

columns.name: flux error
columns.description: propagated SAP error over the median, one sigma, per bin

masks.rule: any nonzero flag drops the cadence
a cadence without a finite value in all three is dropped
a bin with fewer than 3 kept cadences is dropped

reductions: 20-minute bins average up to 10 two-minute cadences each; the transit, about 3.2 hours long, spans nine or ten bins.
Flux is kept to 1 ppm and its error to 5 ppm (binned-relative-flux/1).

source.archive: MAST (Barbara A. Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes)

citations.text: TESS Light Curves - All Sectors, STScI/MAST
Esteves et al. 2015, ApJ 804, 150 (2015ApJ...804..150E): the period and radius ratio the pack is checked against
Shporer et al. 2014, ApJ 788, 92 (2014ApJ...788...92S): the planet orbits Kepler-13A

steps: Read tess2019198215352-s0014-0000000158324245-0150-s_lc.fits with the SDK's readFits(), pinned by its checksum.

Mask, normalize and bin SAP_FLUX with the SDK's binTessLightCurve(), the pipeline every TESS pack uses: QUALITY 0 and finite values only, divided by the median, 20-minute bins of at least 3 cadences; the header's CROWDSAP and FLFRCSAP recorded.

assumptions: SAP flux is the aperture's light as collected: it holds the companion's light as well as A's, so a transit on A is diluted by the fraction CROWDSAP. Systematics are not removed.
Times are barycentric dynamical time for the target, as SPOC corrects them.

Which star the planet orbits is not in these data: 21-arcsecond pixels cannot separate A and B, 1.2 arcseconds apart. That it orbits A comes from other observations (Shporer et al. 2014 and the work it cites).

validation.check: folding on the published period finds the corrected depth times CROWDSAP, within 0.001
